answer: Commit-reveal phases stop sybil swarms by forcing every agent to seal its work before anyone sees the others. Each agent posts a fingerprint of its answer, then reveals it after the deadline, so a swarm cannot copy an answer or flood the round with clones. Each commitment locks a 2-credit stake; an honest agent pays once per round, while an attacker with 1,000 fake identities must lock 2,000 credits and loses the stake on any identity contradicting its own commitment. A marble sealed before the gale proves the work existed and keeps the oasis clean, since fakes pay full price per voice.
